currentContext.expansion: Unimech describes an integrated manufacturing footprint of 2,73,000 sq. ft. across three specialised facilities in Bengaluru: (i) the Aero Tooling Unit, 1,50,000 sq. ft. at Devanahalli Aerospace SEZ, a dedicated facility manufacturing specialised aero-engine and airframe tooling for global aerospace programmes; (ii) the High Precision Components and Assembly Unit, 93,000 sq. ft. at Devanahalli Industrial Area, established to support growing demand for high-precision components, assemblies and mission-critical engineering solutions — commissioned with 33,000 sq. ft. in October 2025 and expanded by an additional 60,000 sq. ft. in January 2026; and (iii) the Central Fabrication Unit, 30,000 sq. ft. at Devanahalli Industrial Area, a dedicated fabrication hub strengthening manufacturing integration and operational agility. Together these form a unified platform supporting complex, high-mix, low-volume production across aerospace, defence, energy, semiconductor and emerging industries. Installed capacity is stated at 6.8 Lakh machine hours (FY 2025-26) with capacity utilisation of 52%, and the Company states it is 'Future Ready' with 4-acre land available to scale operations and enable strategic partnerships. Core capacity levers cited are comprehensive 3, 4 and 5-axis machining, double column milling, turning, EDM and electro-mechanical integration, plus 'significant capacity augmentation through advanced VMCs, HMCs, and boring machines'. Two further units are described beyond Bengaluru: a 2,00,000 sq. ft. facility at Duvvada SEZ, Visakhapatnam dedicated to serving the industrial segment with engineered solutions for power generation, locomotives and industrial infrastructure, supported by an additional 20,000 sq. ft. of warehousing space to enhance operational efficiency, inventory management and scalability; and the Kanoo Unimech Advanced Manufacturing Solutions Unit of 90,000 sq. ft. at Modon Industrial Area, Saudi Arabia — a facility being commissioned to establish advanced precision manufacturing and remanufacturing in Dammam, serving oil & gas, energy, industrial and engineered products sectors across the Kingdom and the broader GCC region. A further heading, 'Hobel Bellows - Engineered Components Unit', appears with no readable body text before the routed extract is cut off. On R&D-led capability build-out, the Company states it invests continuously in product development, advanced manufacturing technologies and strategic collaborations, with focus areas covering a Micro Gas Turbine (MGT) platform (exclusive manufacturing rights through the Dheya Engineering partnership, development of indigenous propulsion technologies, applications across aerospace, defence and unmanned platforms, and expansion into hydrogen propulsion systems), indigenous Electronic Control Unit (ECU) development, engineering excellence (build-to-design, prototyping, design-for-manufacturing optimisation) and a digitally integrated manufacturing ecosystem (ERP-driven planning, automated CNC programming, digital quality workflows and end-to-end traceability). (2) In the extracted two-column layout the unit HEADINGS and their sq. ft. body lines are interleaved; the Duvvada SEZ, Visakhapatnam block appears with no legible heading of its own, the 90,000 sq. ft. Modon/Dammam block is matched to the 'Kanoo Unimech Advanced Manufacturing Solutions Unit' heading on the strength of its own text naming Dammam, Saudi Arabia, and the 'Hobel Bellows - Engineered Components Unit' heading has no accompanying figures in the routed text. No timelines or rupee amounts are stated for the Visakhapatnam, Saudi Arabia or Hobel Bellows units. (3) TRUNCATION: the MD&A extract begins mid-word ('rcraft demand') and ends mid-sentence ('significant investments are also being directed towards'); the R&D/Manufacturing spread begins mid-word ('ring Capabilities') and ends mid-word ('Advanced Precision M'), cutting off the Core Capabilities panel and the Hobel Bellows unit description; the BRSR extract begins mid-word ('ential Indicators') and ends mid-sentence ('at the conclusion of'). (4) NAMED DISCLOSURE DEFECT: the block supplied as '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE — CAPITAL COMMITMENTS ===' carries no capital-commitment figure and no readable column date — it reads verbatim: '[page 253] (All amounts in INR Lakhs, unless otherwise stated) | FOR THE YEAR ENDED MARCH 31, 2026 (CONTD.) | As at / The Group is not subject to any externally imposed capital commitments. / 44'. The dangling 'As at' has no date against it, and the sentence supplied is a capital-MANAGEMENT statement about externally imposed capital requirements, not the 'capital expenditure contracted for but not provided' commitment the heading names; the trailing '44' is an unlabelled fragment (apparently a note number). risks.risk: Global trade policy and tariff exposure / geopolitical developments
risks.note: Named first in the MD&A Risk Management section as 'exposure to global trade policy changes and geopolitical developments'. It is not theoretical for FY 2025-26: the MD&A states 'Elevated U.S. tariff conditions and temporary disruptions across export markets created pressure on customer procurement patterns and revenue realisation', and the Chairman describes ordering patterns that 'remained subdued' for much of the year. Structural because exports are a large share of the business and the largest export market is the one where tariffs bit. Mitigation cited: strengthening geographic and business diversification and expanding customer relationships across new sectors.

risks.risk: Customer concentration within core aerospace programmes
risks.note: Explicitly listed as a key risk in the MD&A Risk Management section. The customer base is small and programme-linked — the Chairman states the Company serves 'approximately 35 customers across North America, Europe and India', and the BRSR (sibling bundle) records that a single activity, manufacturing relating to aero engine tooling and airframe tooling, accounts for 98% of turnover with clientele predominantly global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers. Long qualification cycles cut both ways: they raise switching costs but also make any programme loss slow to replace. PROVENANCE: the 98% single-activity and OEM/Tier-1 clientele figures are back-filled from the BRSR Section A tables, which are present in the profile and governance_entities bundles, not in this one.

Listed as a key risk in the MD&A. Aerospace, defence and nuclear work is gated by certification and qualification regimes; the BRSR stakeholder table records engagement with governmental bodies and authorities to ensure 'compliance with aerospace and defense regulations, environmental requirements, and safety certification standards'. Mitigation cited: maintaining globally recognised quality systems.

risks.risk: Integration risk from strategic initiatives / inorganic expansion
risks.note: Named in the MD&A as 'integration risks associated with strategic initiatives'. The Company is simultaneously integrating and scaling Hobel Bellows (a listed MD&A priority, adding approximately 290 employees), standing up the Saudi JV, and has incorporated Uniflux Renewable Energy — three unrelated integration efforts running at once, in businesses (bellows/metal forming, remanufacturing, renewable-energy EPC) adjacent to but distinct from the tooling core.

risks.risk: Operational complexity of a high-mix, low-volume manufacturing environment
risks.note: Named in the MD&A as 'operational complexities arising from a high-mix manufacturing environment'. The Company describes a qualified ecosystem of more than 5,900 SKUs and 'complex, high-mix, low-volume production', which raises scheduling, tooling-changeover and quality-traceability burden per unit of revenue. Mitigation cited: ERP, MES deployment, CMM-integrated quality systems and monitoring of machining efficiency through a right-first-time approach and dispatch-cycle discipline.

Named in the MD&A as 'increasing cybersecurity considerations linked to digital adoption', and echoed in the Board's Report risk policy which explicitly lists cyber risk. It matters because the Company's model depends on secure digital systems for customer collaboration, documentation exchange and quality traceability, and clients themselves raised 'the importance of data security' in the BRSR stakeholder engagement table. Mitigation cited: continued investment in digital infrastructure, predictive maintenance, advanced analytics and cybersecurity infrastructure.

risks.risk: Very high employee attrition and dependence on specialised technical talent
risks.note: A structural concentration risk the AR discloses without labelling it a risk: the BRSR turnover-rate table records permanent-employee turnover of 49.06% in FY 2025-26 (57.53% in FY 2024-25) and permanent-worker turnover of 13.79% (75.00% in FY 2024-25). The MD&A itself calls the workforce 'a key competitive advantage' resting on 'specialised technical expertise', and the industry outlook names 'availability of skilled talent' as a key industry challenge. The Company also churned its Company Secretary twice inside two years. Mitigation cited: structured onboarding, cross-functional training, performance-linked incentives, ESOP-based employee ownership and an integrated HRMS. PROVENANCE: the turnover-rate percentages are back-filled from BRSR Section A item 22, present in the profile and governance_entities bundles, not in this one.

risks.risk: Low capacity utilisation / operating-leverage risk after a capex-heavy year
risks.note: The MD&A lists 'Improving capacity utilisation and operating leverage' as a forward priority and notes 'significant manufacturing headroom', while the Corporate Overview discloses capacity utilisation of 52% against installed capacity of 6.8 Lakh machine hours. Capacity was added into a soft-demand year — a precision components & assemblies facility and a fabrication facility commissioned in October, with a further 60,000 sq. ft. added in January 2026 — so fixed-cost absorption depends on the demand normalisation management describes as under way rather than as achieved. PROVENANCE: the 52% utilisation and facility dates are back-filled from the Corporate Overview 'Our Manufacturing Prowess' spread supplied in the capex_expansion bundle.

The BRSR 'Openness of business' table records purchases from trading houses at 70% of total purchases (67% prior year) sourced from 78 trading houses versus 185 a year earlier, with the top 10 accounting for 41% of those purchases (34% prior year) — a materially narrower supplier base year on year. The MD&A industry commentary independently flags raw-material constraints, production bottlenecks and supply-chain vulnerability across the A&D ecosystem. PROVENANCE: the concentration percentages are back-filled from BRSR Principle 1 item 9, supplied in the capex_expansion bundle, not in this one.

one-line thesis: High-margin, capability-led precision tooling/components platform recovering from a tariff-hit FY26, pivoting to a multi-pillar (tooling + precision components + nuclear + Saudi JV + Hobel) growth story for FY27 with order book doubled to ~Rs.314cr.
scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | FY26 (full year) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (net of tariff concession) | ~Rs.82cr | ~Rs.240cr | Gross FY26 ~Rs.257cr; Q4 gross ~Rs.96-97cr |
| Gross margin | ~73% | ~70% | Tooling-led |
| EBITDA margin | ~43% | ~31% | Assess Q3+Q4 together (cost absorbed in Q3) |
| PAT | ~Rs.26cr | ~Rs.63cr | FY26 PAT below last year |
| Other income | — | ~Rs.47cr (+~90% YoY) | Treasury; will moderate in FY27 post-M&A deployment |
| ROCE / ROE | 22% / 26% (qtr) | 10% / 16% (FY) | Standalone pre-acq was >50% ROCE |
| Order book (May'26, consol incl. Hobel) | ~Rs.314cr | — | >2x historical; ex-Hobel ~Rs.200cr+ |
| Finance cost | — | ~Rs.15.3cr | Incl. Rs.9.6cr one-time FX loss; underlying ~Rs.5.7cr |
| Plant utilization | ~50% | — | FA turnover ~1.4x |
| Working capital days | — | ~120-125 | May drift to 150-160 with project mix |
guidance:
- No formal numeric guidance. Q1 FY27 revenue targeted to **surpass Q4 FY26** (~Rs.82cr net baseline); healthy improvement over Q4 expected.
- FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin "better than FY26" (~31%), but Kanoo JV start-up will pull full-year margin; mgmt guides "similar margin profile" pragmatically.
- ~5% tariff sharing on US-consumed parts/tooling expected to persist (manageable).
- Nuclear orders to execute largely H2 FY27.
- FAI target: double the ~200 done in FY26.
order book:
- ~Rs.314cr consol (incl. Hobel ~Rs.107cr); ex-Hobel ~Rs.200cr+.
- Composition: tooling ~Rs.100cr+; nuclear ~Rs.87cr to date (from near-zero last year); rest precision components (small but scaling).
- Execution windows: aero tooling 4-6 months (recurring, PO-to-PO); nuclear 12-18 months; Hobel ~12-month visibility.
segment:
- Aero engine/airframe complex tooling ~90% of Q4 and FY26 revenue — core; remains export-heavy (~90% exports).
- Precision components/assemblies + nuclear PCA (turnkey systems) = stated growth engine; biggest buildup expected from precision parts then nuclear.
- ~6,000 qualified SKUs; >200 FAIs across aero/semi/defense.
growth:
- Q4 sequential recovery driven by aerospace tooling normalization + release of deferred orders.
- New aerospace customer onboarded; more in pipeline. Nuclear (EMCCR Tarapur/Madras) ramping; new tenders (incl. MP) awaited via L&T/Megha-type EPCs.
- Hobel cross-sell into nuclear (bellows for reactor/cooler systems), then aero/semi over medium-long term.
- Dheya: DET-500 micro gas turbine 90% load validation, 500+ min runtime; DET-200 certification on track; initial 2-engine defense orders, scalable to ~200; Unimech is exclusive mfg partner.
margins:
- Gross margin structurally high (70-73%) on tooling mix. EBITDA ~31% FY26 (Q4 flattered by Q3 cost-loading).
- Employee cost ~22% of rev (grew 16%); opex ~16% (grew 28%) — both to trend down as revenue scales. Subcontracting ~6%. Depreciation ~Rs.7cr/qtr.
- Hobel acquired for capability, NOT margin profile — likely margin-dilutive; Kanoo JV start-up dilutive on consol margins.
capex:
- No major core-business capex foreseen in FY27 (>150 CNC machines installed in Bangalore; new facility commissioned in FY26).
- Saudi Kanoo JV: $30m total joint investment (Unimech 51% = ~$15.3m), mostly capex/infra over first 3 years; meaningful capex hits FY27.
- FTWZ fully approved (SEZ clearance + ICEGATE final stage).
capital allocation:
- Rs.450cr cash deployed for Hobel (via subsidiary) — at consol shows as goodwill/intangible, NOT amortized/expensed; EPS accretive.
- Treasury yielded ~Rs.47cr other income FY26; will moderate as funds deployed into M&A.
- No dividend mention; capital directed to inorganic capability + JV.
risks:
- US tariff overhang (residual ~5% sharing); customer inventory cycles; geopolitical/GCC conflicts.
- ~90% export concentration; aerospace OEM/engine maker dependence; lumpy PO-to-PO tooling.
- Low utilization (~50%), FA turnover 1.4x — operating leverage unproven at scale.
- Goodwill-heavy balance sheet depresses ROCE/ROE near term (10%/16%).
- Long aerospace qualification cycles (2-3yr) for Hobel cross-sell; AS9100 + NADCAP pending (6-9 months for AS9100).
- Kanoo JV ~3-year breakeven, margin drag.
mgmt tone: Constructively optimistic; candid on FY26 being a "defining/foundation" year rather than high-growth. Transparent on tariff-driven revenue shortfall (defended the 90-100cr guidance as met on gross basis). Pushed back politely against analyst skepticism on legacy organic growth. Repeated "platform/capability-led" framing.
non-obvious:
- The much-touted ~Rs.314cr order book is ~Rs.107cr Hobel + ~Rs.87cr nuclear; ex-those, legacy tooling order book is roughly flat YoY — analyst (Garvit Goyal) pressed that ex-Hobel Q1 FY27 implies legacy ~Rs.50-60cr, similar to last year. Mgmt deflected.
- One customer is reportedly insourcing MRO tooling; mgmt denies structural loss.
- Hobel rationale is the larger precision-component/assembly TAM, not aero tooling.
- Domestic aerospace will stay small (no Indian airframe OEM); defense is the only meaningful domestic upside.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Nuclear capacity expansion (EMCCR, NPCIL) | beneficiary | Unimech Aerospace | UNIMECH | 544322 | Nuclear sub-assembly/turnkey supplier | Med | self | ~Rs.87cr wins, H2 FY27 execution |
| Defence propulsion (Dheya micro gas turbine) | beneficiary | Unimech Aerospace | UNIMECH | 544322 | Exclusive mfg partner (30% stake in Dheya) | Med | self | Scalable to ~200 engines if qualified |
| Domestic nuclear EPC tenders (new reactors, MP) | beneficiary | Larsen & Toubro | LT | 500510 | Nuclear EPC prime; Unimech sub-supplies | Med | external | Named by mgmt as likely prime |
| Domestic nuclear EPC tenders | beneficiary | Megha Engineering | (unverified) | (code unverified) | Nuclear EPC prime (unlisted) | Low | external | "Mega" cited by mgmt |
| US tariffs on aerospace imports | loser | Unimech Aerospace | UNIMECH | 544322 | ~5% tariff sharing, FY26 concessions | Med | self | Rs.~16cr gross-to-net haircut FY26 |
| Customer MRO-tooling insourcing | loser | Unimech Aerospace | UNIMECH | 544322 | Risk of tooling revenue erosion | Low | self | Mgmt denies structural loss |
qoq change log:
- vs Q3 FY26: Sharp sequential recovery — Q4 net rev ~Rs.82cr (gross ~Rs.96-97cr) vs subdued Q3; EBITDA margin jumped to ~43% (but flattered by Q3 cost-loading — view H2 together).
- Order book roughly doubled to ~Rs.314cr (consol, incl. Hobel) — Hobel ~Rs.107cr added; nuclear scaled to ~Rs.87cr.
- Hobel Bellows acquisition closed Apr'26 (~Rs.450cr) — to consolidate from Q1 FY27.
- Kanoo Saudi JV: Ministry of Investment approval received; $30m plan, capex in FY27.
- FTWZ: all approvals received (vs in-progress earlier); ICEGATE in final enablement.
- Tariffs moderated from elevated levels seen earlier in FY26; order inflows normalizing.
- New aerospace customer onboarded during FY26.

hero.oneLiner: Unimech Aerospace is a Bengaluru-based precision engineering company that has evolved beyond aerospace tooling into an integrated engineering platform serving aerospace, defence, nuclear energy, semiconductors and industrial manufacturing.
